questions.q: What is the main event that starts the plot of the Dr. Dolittle story?
questions.a: The story begins when the Cat's-food-Man suggests that the doctor should stop treating people and become an animal doctor. A wrong answer here shows the student has not yet identified the 'inciting incident' or the spark that sets the story in motion.

questions.q: In your own words, why is it considered humorous that a doctor talks to animals?
questions.a: It is funny because we expect doctors to treat humans in clinics, not animals in nature. A wrong answer suggests the student is looking for 'jokes' rather than understanding that humour often comes from 'absurd' or unexpected role-reversals.

questions.q: If a doctor suddenly started asking a stray dog about its stomach ache, what part of the 'humour' criteria would this satisfy?
questions.a: This satisfies the 'reversal of roles' criteria, as the animal becomes the patient. A wrong answer shows confusion between a 'funny situation' and a 'character trait.'

questions.q: Compare the doctor's interaction with humans versus his interaction with animals. How does this drive the plot?
questions.a: The doctor moves from a traditional medical practice to a new, strange one, creating the central conflict and progression of the story. A wrong answer suggests the student sees the events as random rather than a chain of cause-and-effect.

questions.q: Do you think the animals' observations about humans make the story better? Why or why not?
questions.a: Yes, because it gives a 'fresh perspective' on human habits, making the reader laugh at themselves. A wrong answer indicates the student hasn't considered the author's purpose in adding these observations.

questions.q: Imagine a new scene where Dr. Dolittle tries to give a parrot medicine. How would you make this scene humorous?
questions.a: The scene could be humorous if the parrot tries to tell the doctor how to be a better doctor or critiques the medicine. A poor answer would just be a standard description of a medical check-up without any 'absurd' or 'role-reversal' elements.
